# local 0001: Pointers to void, int, or long that are initialized with a string literal get bytes of a host address

- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Confirm the two choices under Decision and apply the patch.
- Patch: [local-0001.patch](../../patches/local-0001.patch), commit [`7cf38723d`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/7cf38723d5a5ed03de20731433d53ff98105bd32). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For pointers to `void`, `int`, or `long` that are initialized by data with a string literal, the
compiler writes bytes of an address in its own memory where the address of the string belongs.
The file below was compiled on r17176 with `sdcc -mmcs51 --model-large wide.c`.

```c
#pragma disable_warning 244

__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[2];

int const *wide = L"AB";

void main (void)
{
  res[0] = *wide;               /* 0x41 expected */
  res[1] = 0x55;                /* main ran to its end */
}
```

The assembly has `.byte #0x30,#0x6e,#0x62` at `__xinit__wide`. `wchar_t` is `unsigned long` in
SDCC, and the pragma disables the warning for the difference between the type of the pointer and
the type of the literal. The bytes change from one run of the compiler to the next. In ucsim,
`res[0]` was `89` after one compile and `ff` after another.

On mcs51 the fault occurs for objects in xdata that have an initial value and for `const` objects
with every model. With `--model-small` and `--model-medium` the compiler initializes the pointer
above by code that loads the address of the string, and `res[0]` is `41`. Struct members and
array elements of these pointer types get such bytes too. So do pointers that are initialized
with a narrow literal, as in `const void * const p = "AB";`. When only `const` objects of these
pointer types refer to a literal, the string is absent from the assembly.

## Cause

`printIvalPtr` in `src/SDCCglue.c` passes the value to `printIvalCharPtr`, which prints the label
of the string, only when the pointer in the declaration points to a character type or to an
unsigned `int` type of any length. For a string literal, `constExprValue` returns a value that has
the storage class `S_LITERAL` and the name of the string. The numeric members of its union overlap
`v_char`, the compiler's pointer to the characters. For the other pointer types `printIvalPtr`
executes its `IS_LITERAL` branch, which prints the low bytes of that pointer with `aopLiteral`.
Under gdb on r17176, `v_char` was `0x56091d912c50`, and the compiler wrote `50 2c 91`.
`printIvalCharPtr` is also the only function that adds strings to `ccpStr`, the set that
`emitStaticSeg` consults before it emits a string.

## Fix

`printIvalPtr` also passes to `printIvalCharPtr` each value for which `IS_LITERAL` holds and whose
symbol is a string literal. The change is one condition.

## Decision

The condition requires `IS_LITERAL`. String literals behind a cast, with an offset, or behind `&`
reach `printIvalPtr` as values for which it does not hold, and their strings stay absent from the
assembly, as the last item under Related describes. With a condition on the symbol alone, the
compiler emits these strings. A file that initializes one pointer with `"YZ"` and another with
`(int const *) "YZ"` then got the label of the string twice. By the source, the cause is the copy
of the symbol that the second item under Related describes.

The type check of `printIvalPtr` follows the call and is skipped for these values, as it is for
character pointers. Without the patch, that check gives warning 18, "Initializer different levels
of indirections", on mcs51 for pointers to `void` in code memory, such as
`const void __code * const p = "AB";`. With the patch the declaration compiles without a
diagnostic. The alternative is to keep the check for these values, and the warning with it.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/strlit-ptr-init.c` initializes pointers to `void`, `int`, and `long`
with narrow and wide literals, as objects, `const` objects, struct members, and array elements.
Compiled by r17192, it fails 18 of its 34 assertions on mcs51-small, mcs51-medium, and
mcs51-small-stack-auto, and 30 on mcs51-large, mcs51-huge, and mcs51-large-stack-auto. It fails
22 of 30 on stm8 and 23 of 30 on ucz80. With the patch it passes on these eight targets and on
host. `support/valdiag/tests/strlit-ptr-init.c` has four declarations of pointers to `void`.
Without the patch it gets warning 18 for mcs51, and with the patch it compiles without a
diagnostic.

With the patch, the assembly of the other regression tests is unchanged for mcs51-small. For
mcs51-large it differs in `p99-conformance.c`, where two pointers to wide literals get the
address of their string. With the patch series of this report up to this patch applied to r17192,
the regression suite ran without a failure for host, the six mcs51 variants above, stm8, and
ucz80. The diagnostics suite ran without a failure for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80,
and stm8.

## Related

- In the test case of bug #3973, the `const void *` member gets the label of the string with the
  patch on mcs51, stm8, and z80. Its `uint32_t` member, which `printIvalType` prints, gets bytes
  of a host address with this patch alone. The patch for bug #3973 corrects that member.
- The output for `char const * const cp = (char const *) "CD";` does not assemble, on r17192 and
  with the patch, because the label of the string is defined twice. By the source, `initValPointer`
  copies the value and its symbol with `copyValue`, `printIvalCharPtr` adds the copy to
  `statsg->syms`, and `emitStaticSeg` emits both symbols. This was not confirmed in a debugger.
- With and without the patch, `int const * const p = (int const *) L"IJ";`,
  `void const * const p = "UV" + 1;`, and `char const (* const p)[3] = &"WX";` refer to the label
  of a string that is absent from the assembly unless a character pointer refers to that literal.
